newsitem.title: UK: LCE coffee ends off highs as resistance weighs.
newsitem.headline: LCE coffee ends off highs as resistance weighs.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures ended firmer but saw earlier gains sliced as New York staged a correction from Monday's highs.
"There is nothing really supportive in London," said one trader. "Even when New York was going up, London had no fund buying coming through," he said.
The only buyers in London were linked to arbitrage business against New York, traders said.
At the close, the benchmark November contract stood just below the $1,700 mark at $1,690 a tonne, $23 higher on the day after reaching a session peak of $1,740 at the opening.
But London's reluctance to go higher was witnessed earlier as it snubbed the technical call to open $140 higher and rose only $73 at the start.
Technical resistance was mainly blamed for capping the gains with a band of heavy supply weighing on the market up to $1,800.
"We have to get up to $1,800 and see how it does there," said one trader.
But unless fund buying kicked in, there was no incentive to chase the market higher, he added.
Nearby supply worries buoyed New York on Monday as the front September contract soared to a one-year high.
A correction was expected on Tuesday but traders said the overall trend in New York remained upward while a total of only four delivery notices were issued on against a large open interest.
